blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — A resolution seeking an investigation into the implementation of the No Contact Apprehension Policy (NCAP) to ensure fairness to motorists cited for traffic violations despite poor road infrastructure has been filed in the Senate. Senate Resolution No. 732, filed by Sen. Robin Padilla on Oct. 12, seeks an inquiry into fairness and due process in NCAP’s implementation following multiple complaints involving poorly maintained roads and other infrastructure. “The effectiveness of automated traffic enforcement depends on clear road signs, visible lane markings, properly functioning traffic signals, and adequate road infrastructure to ensure that motorists can reasonably comply with traffic […]...
